lines.text: What if everything cost exactly the same?
A pack of gum, a phone and a car. All one price.
Hour one. You walk into the mall, and anything big is suddenly a bargain.
Phones and TVs sell out in minutes.

segments.caption: Small things cost a fortune
segments.fact: A BOTTLE OF WATER = A TV

lines.text: Day one. But a bottle of water now costs as much as a TV.
A pack of gum is a luxury, and nobody buys small things anymore.

segments.caption: Shops get clever
segments.fact: ONE PRICE = ONE CRATE OF SNACKS

lines.text: Day two. Shops get clever. One price now buys a whole crate of snacks,

segments.caption: Factories stop
segments.fact: EVERY CAR SOLD AT A LOSS

lines.text: Week one. Car makers lose money on every car they sell, so the factories stop, and the showroom stays empty.
Month one. Shelves are bare, queues stretch through the mall, and people start swapping things instead.

segments.caption: A price control
segments.fact: MOST ECONOMISTS: PRICE CAPS CAUSE SHORTAGES

lines.text: Economists call this a price control, and most agree caps like this cause shortages, just like the queues in the Soviet Union.
Prices tell everyone what's rare and what's worth making.
So, what would you buy first?
